problem.text: Two circles of radius $5$ are externally tangent to each other and are internally tangent to a circle of radius $13$ at points $A$ and $B$, as shown in the diagram. The distance $AB$ can be written in the form $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. What is $m+n$?

steps.title: Where to start: connect the centers
steps.body: Every length we are given is a radius of a tangent circle, so name the centers: $M$ for the big circle, $N$ for the left small circle, $O$ for the right small circle. When one circle touches another from inside, the line through their centers passes through the touching point. So $M$, $N$, $A$ lie on one line with $N$ between $M$ and $A$, and likewise $M$, $O$, $B$.

your_turn.answer: $8$, because $MA = 13$ is a radius of the big circle and $NA = 5$ is a radius of the small one, so $MN = 13 - 5$.

steps.title: Collect the lengths
steps.body: In the same way $MO = 8$, and $MA = MB = 13$. The two small circles touch from outside, so the segment $NO$ passes through their touching point.

your_turn.answer: $10$, the sum of the two radii $5 + 5$.

steps.title: Spot the similar triangles
steps.body:
Compare triangle $MNO$ with triangle $MAB$. The sides at $M$ are in the same ratio: $\frac{MN}{MA} = \frac{MO}{MB} = \frac{8}{13}$. The angle between them is the same angle, so the triangles are similar by SAS, with $N$ matching $A$ and $O$ matching $B$. That means $NO$ matches $AB$:
$$\frac{NO}{AB} = \frac{MN}{MA}$$

your_turn.prompt: Why is angle $NMO$ the very same angle as angle $AMB$?
your_turn.answer: $N$ lies on segment $MA$ and $O$ lies on segment $MB$, so both angles are formed by the same two rays from $M$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: So $\frac{10}{AB} = \frac{8}{13}$, which gives $AB = \frac{130}{8} = \frac{65}{4}$. Since $65 = 5\cdot 13$ and $4 = 2^2$ share no factor, $m = 65$ and $n = 4$, and $m + n = 69$. The answer is **(D)**.
